tasks.prompt: The printed entry gives drīfan, drāf, drifon, drifen. Label the four principal-part positions. Which two entries are finite indicative forms, and which two are nonfinite citations?
tasks.target_specification: Four principal-part positions, with supplied infinitive/participle citations distinguished from productive finite preterites.

tasks.prompt: Using the printed principal-part table, identify the strong class of rīdan, bēodan and bindan. For each verb give the second-person singular preterite and state which principal-part stem it uses.
tasks.target_specification: Strong second-singular preterite uses the plural-preterite stem plus -e, not the first/third-singular preterite stem.

tasks.prompt: Give every person and number represented by the finite forms drāf and drifon in the selected indicative paradigm. Explain why the supplied citation drifen is not another person of that paradigm.
tasks.target_specification: Syncretic first/third singular and all three plural persons; past participle citation does not become finite or confer passive/perfect syntax.

tasks.prompt: Compare ðū ride and ðū hīerdest. Give the person, number and tense of each verb, and explain the different formation of their preterites.
tasks.target_specification: Strong versus already taught weak preterite; short i in ride, dental preterite of hīeran.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of drīfan. Label all three persons in the singular and plural even where forms coincide.
tasks.target_specification: Complete Class I ordinary model, including strong second-singular preterite.

tasks.prompt: For rīdan and wrītan, give the first-, second- and third-person singular present, then the first- and second-person singular preterite and the plural preterite. Explain the selected present dental forms.
tasks.target_specification: Class I d/t present contractions with the full ablaut relation; selected spelling and admitted variants remain distinct.

tasks.prompt: For rīsan and snīðan, give the second- and third-person singular present and the second-person singular and plural preterite. Identify the consonant change in snīðan.
tasks.target_specification: Class I s-stem present and ð/d grammatical alternation; no unrestricted change in every ð-stem.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of wrēon. Keep its contracted present forms distinct from its preterite stems.
tasks.target_specification: Full Class I contracted pattern; no imperative or nonfinite syntax test.

tasks.prompt: Translate “I rode. You rode. He rode. We rode.” Address one person in the second sentence. Then give the four corresponding present-tense sentences.
tasks.target_specification: Present/past and person contrasts of rīdan without an unassigned goal or transport construction.

tasks.prompt: With drīfan, give the present forms agreeing with ic, wē, ðū and hē. Then give the corresponding preterite forms. Keep the person and number of each subject unchanged.
tasks.target_specification: Agreement and stem selection through all assigned finite persons; morphology only, with no new object frame implied.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of bēodan. Identify the present forms whose vowel differs from that of the infinitive citation.
tasks.target_specification: Complete Class II ēo pattern, present mutation and selected d-stem endings.

tasks.prompt: For būgan, give the first-, second- and third-person singular present and the second-person singular and plural preterite. Contrast its present vowel change with bēodan.
tasks.target_specification: Class II ū → ȳ in selected second/third present, contrasted with ēo → īe; no object or bowing complement inferred.

tasks.prompt: For cēosan, give the second- and third-person singular present, the first- and second-person singular preterite and the plural preterite. Explain where the selected s and r occur.
tasks.target_specification: Class II s/r alternation and finite diagnostic cells; no recall of the participle citation required.

tasks.prompt: For sēoðan and drēogan, give the second- and third-person singular present, the first- and second-person singular preterite and the plural preterite. Keep the two verbs’ consonant patterns distinct.
tasks.target_specification: Class II ð/d alternation versus audited present g/h options; full lexical diagnostic mapping.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of tēon, “draw”. Use the Class II verb assigned in this unit.
tasks.target_specification: Full Class II contracted pattern; the English sense identifies the assigned homograph.

tasks.prompt: Compare the assigned wrēon and tēon tables. Give each verb’s first-person singular present, first-person singular preterite, second-person singular preterite and plural preterite. Explain why the similar infinitive endings do not make them members of the same strong class.
tasks.target_specification: Two complete contracted systems distinguished by principal-part series; nonfinite citations supplied as table headings.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of bindan. Explain the selected second- and third-person singular present forms.
tasks.target_specification: Complete nasal Class III model, bintst/bint dental cluster outcomes and two preterite stems.

tasks.prompt: For helpan and gieldan, give the second- and third-person singular present, the first- and second-person singular preterite and the plural preterite. Preserve each verb’s selected stem vowels.
tasks.target_specification: Class III el and iel families with their exact present and preterite forms.

tasks.prompt: For weorpan and berstan, give the second- and third-person singular present, the first- and second-person singular preterite and the plural preterite. Explain the difference between their first preterite stems.
tasks.target_specification: Class III eor and metathesized berst patterns; short vowels and selected -st outcomes.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of weorðan. Identify the cells with ð and those with d.
tasks.target_specification: Complete weorðan indicative and grammatical alternation; passive use remains outside production.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of findan. State the ordinary third-person singular preterite selected here and its documented alternative. Then give the second- and third-person singular present and plural preterite of winnan.
tasks.target_specification: Findan person-specific selected funde and admitted fand; no claim that first-person funde is impossible. Winnan nn simplification.

tasks.prompt: For drincan and singan, give the second- and third-person singular present, the first- and second-person singular preterite and the plural preterite. State which Class III pattern they follow.
tasks.target_specification: Narrative lexical applications of the bindan family, with exact finite cells.

tasks.prompt: Give the complete selected present and preterite indicative of tōberstan and forweorðan. Identify the base pattern used by each, and give the separately learned meaning of each whole verb.
tasks.target_specification: Full separately audited prefixed source verbs; no productive prefix or meaning rule.

tasks.prompt: Consult the complete reference tables of bregdan and fēolan. Identify their third-person singular present and plural preterite entries and the special changes noted with them. These are recognition reference forms.
tasks.target_specification: Recognition of two complete rare exceptional patterns from displayed tables; no unaided recall or unassigned clause government.

tasks.prompt: Give the nominative, genitive, dative and accusative singular and plural of scip and wind. Explain their different nominative and accusative plural endings.
tasks.target_specification: Complete short neuter scip and strong masculine wind, based on previously taught nominal classes.

tasks.prompt: Give the nominative, genitive, dative and accusative singular and plural of strand and gefēra. Explain why gefēran alone does not identify a unique case and number.
tasks.target_specification: Complete strong masculine strand and weak masculine gefēra; syncretism interpreted through context.

tasks.prompt: Translate “The companions found two ships on the shore. The good man’s ship was small.” In the second sentence put the limiting genitive before the head noun.
tasks.target_specification: New noun senses/cells in prior locative and nested genitive constructions; on describes the ships’ location, not a goal.

tasks.prompt: Translate “The companions choose the small dwelling. We choose the great ship.”
tasks.target_specification: Cēosan with an audited accusative thing chosen; adjective/article agreement.

tasks.prompt: Translate “The man found the good man’s ship. He bound the animal.” Put the limiting genitive before its head noun.
tasks.target_specification: Audited findan and bindan accusative objects with prior nested genitive and personal reference.

tasks.prompt: Translate “We two drank the water, and you two sang well.” Retain both dual subjects.
tasks.target_specification: Dual personal subjects with plural strong preterites, accusative drink and intransitive singing with prior manner adverb.

tasks.prompt: Change the subjects to the corresponding plurals and make the verbs agree: Se mann bint ðæt dēor. Se fugol singð wel. Keep the object of the first sentence singular.
tasks.target_specification: Subject versus object number; strong present agreement and ordinary intransitive singing.

tasks.prompt: Change Ic rīde wīde and finde ān hof to the preterite. Preserve the first-person subject, the object and the coordination.
tasks.target_specification: Mixed Class I/III preterite narration with an understood shared subject; selected first-singular fand.

tasks.prompt: Here hē and the companion are different people. Change Hē sang wel, and se gefēra hīerde hine to the present. Identify the subject of each verb and the referent of hine.
tasks.target_specification: Strong and weak present/preterite contrast, with explicit two-person reference; singer is the heard object.

tasks.prompt: Translate “The companion became glad. The companions become glad.” Explain the case and number of the predicate adjectives.
tasks.target_specification: New ordinary become + nominative predicate adjective, explicitly distinct from a passive auxiliary.

tasks.prompt: Translate “I helped the old man. The old man helped me.” Use the case required by the taught helpan construction.
tasks.target_specification: Audited dative recipient of help; no claim that every strong verb takes an accusative object.

tasks.prompt: Translate “The companions did not find the ship. I do not choose the great dwelling.”
tasks.target_specification: Explicitly taught ne with noncontracting strong finite forms; no negative concord or contracted copula.

tasks.prompt: Translate “You did not drink the water. You drink water.” Address one person in the first sentence and several people in the second.
tasks.target_specification: Negation, second-singular strong preterite and second-plural present; person/number marked by pronouns and finite forms.

tasks.prompt: Translate the complete new account “Two companions choose a dwelling”. Preserve the sequence of actions and the speakers in the closing quotation.
tasks.target_specification: Independent connected controlled reading using only productive lexical forms, senses and constructions.

tasks.prompt: List the strong finite verbs in the account. Give each verb’s headword, class, person, number and tense.
tasks.target_specification: Actual strong forms distinguished from prior weak verbs and the copula.

tasks.prompt: For ridon, fundon, curon and druncon in the account, give the corresponding third-person singular preterite and the second-person singular preterite. Preserve the selected lexical exceptions.
tasks.target_specification: Plural-to-singular ablaut and person distinctions; selected findan third singular funde.

tasks.prompt: Which dwelling do the companions choose? Who sings in the quotation, and whom does the addressee hear? Explain the reference of wit, ic, ðū and mē.
tasks.target_specification: Events and pronoun reference; wit includes speaker and one companion, quoted first/second persons shift with speaker.

tasks.prompt: Retell the first four sentences of the account in the present. Preserve the people, things, case relations and adjective endings.
tasks.target_specification: Complete taught strong present narration plus prior copula; no altered story referents.

tasks.prompt: Replace the closing quotation with “We have a good dwelling. We sing, and you hear us.” Let a group of speakers address another group; use plural personal pronouns.
tasks.target_specification: First/second plural strong and weak agreement; new exact speech context prevents arbitrary dual/plural reinterpretation.

tasks.prompt: Translate the complete source passage “The shipwreck and the survivor”, using the local support. Preserve the contrasting fates of the ship, the companions and Apollonius.
tasks.target_specification: Complete supported original episode; supplied later-class finite forms and whole adjunct constructions remain supported.

tasks.prompt: Analyse tōbærst and forwurdon: give each whole verb’s headword, class, person, number and tense, and identify its subject in the passage.
tasks.target_specification: Two new productive prefixed Class III forms with separately taught lexical meanings and subject agreement.

tasks.prompt: Using the proper-name note, distinguish the first Apollonius from the second. Explain why gefēran takes plural forwurdon rather than a singular verb.
tasks.target_specification: Supplied Latin proper-name genitive contrasts with nominative survivor; independently taught weak noun and strong agreement.

tasks.prompt: Identify windas, wind, scip, gefēran and strande in their clauses. Give each noun’s case and number; use the supplied phrase notes wherever the construction is new.
tasks.target_specification: New complete noun forms in contextual analysis; no unassisted government inference for supplied construction.

tasks.prompt: How does Apollonius reach land, and where does the passage leave him? Explain the contribution of the supplied āna without treating it as an ordinary cardinal “one”.
tasks.target_specification: Supported means, motion and alone constructions; distinction from prior cardinal morphology and limited numeral scope.

tasks.prompt: Correct the three marked finite forms: Ðū *drāf. Hīe *cēas ðæt scip. Se mann *bindað ðæt dēor. Preserve the given subjects and tenses.
tasks.target_specification: Second-singular strong preterite, plural preterite ablaut, singular present agreement; literal asterisks mark errors.

tasks.prompt: Write four connected Old English sentences about two companions: they ride, find two ships, choose the small ship, and drink water. Narrate all four actions in the preterite and retain the same two people as subjects.
tasks.target_specification: Open bounded narrative with four taught strong actions and explicit meaning targets; no unique mandatory wording.

tasks.prompt: Translate “The old companion helps my birds. My birds sing well. We found his small ship on the shore.” Distinguish the helper, the birds, the finders and the owner.
tasks.target_specification: Cumulative dative help, agreeing and invariant possessors, strong actions, adjective conditions and locative dative.

tasks.prompt: Analyse Hē funde, Ðū funde and Hīe fundon. Which finite forms distinguish number? What identifies the different persons in the two singular clauses?
tasks.target_specification: Person syncretism created by the selected third-singular funde alongside ordinary second-singular funde; explicit pronouns identify the person.
